analysis.title: GS Flow of Funds: Chopsgiving (Gail Hafif, 16 Nov 2026)
key_insights: GS expects equities to grind moderately higher from here, with bumps. The next two weeks still carry turbulence, but systematic flows are skewed to the upside for the first time in weeks and retail and corporates have held their bid.
Flows are bifurcated. Net weekly and monthly numbers look tame against violent day-to-day reversals. Institutions sold tech and cut leverage while retail bought, so GS calls it a trader's market.

On the GS prime book, Info Tech was the most net sold global and US sector for another week. The US Info Tech long/short ratio is 1.5, versus a YTD peak of 2.14 in early June, and is the lowest on record (since 2016).
US Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 1.6 pts to 209.1% (34th percentile one-year). Net leverage rose 2.1 pts to 45.4% (4th percentile one-year), so institutional positioning is light.

US-listed ETF shorts fell 8.6%, the largest percentage covering in 7 months, led by Large Cap Equity, Credit and Tech ETFs. Single stocks were heavily net sold again (-1.7 SDs one-year), mainly through short sales, which GS reads as active winner-versus-loser selection.

US-listed equity ETFs took in $59.3bn last week, beating 91% of the 46 weeks this year. Fixed income inflows fell to $2.6bn from $13.7bn, with net outflows Thursday and Friday after the hotter-than-expected CPI print.
Semis ETFs lost $7.3bn last week, including $5.6bn on Monday alone, against an average weekly inflow of $6.2bn over the prior four weeks. Plain semis ETFs (SOXX, SMH) barely moved over two weeks.

Levered semis ETFs swung hard. SOXL took in $5.10bn in the Nov 5 week, then lost $4.17bn the next week, its largest weekly outflow in a year. SOXS lost $4.38bn over two weeks and cut its share count by two-thirds. GS reads this as investors lacking conviction and being forced to move with the market.

Global equity funds had net inflows of $98bn in the week ending Nov 11 (vs $89bn prior), led by US funds. Foreign flows have returned to the US, consistent with election-year history, lifting the 4-week average by about $5bn. Money market fund assets fell $18bn.

Retail net bought $6.19bn of US equities, the largest week since Sep 1, with buying concentrated in semis and mega-cap tech. Nvidia (+$1.75bn), AMD (+$672mm), Micron (+$526mm) and Tesla (+$523mm) led. GS flags that losing retail support could change the setup for US equities into year-end.

Corporate buybacks are active, with desk volumes at 1.3x versus both 2025 and 2024 YTD ADTV, skewed to Industrials, Energy and Financials. About 94% of the S&P 500 is in an open window, and GS expects the window to stay open until December 13. 2026 YTD authorizations are $1.52T versus $1.27T in 2025.

CTAs sold over $22bn of S&P in the past week and sold almost $2.5bn of Nasdaq, taking US equity positioning to about -$10bn short, the lowest since April. With vol down from its highs and spot rebounding, they are projected to be buyers in a flat tape, about $10bn of US equities over the next week.

Vol control and risk parity funds sold over $30bn combined over the past week. Risk parity is cutting because stocks and bonds fell together after CPI, but GS does not expect it to be dramatic. Vol control may re-risk in December/January if the market calms.

The GS Panic Index is 6.3/10 (67th percentile, 1y lookback), led by VIX volatility and SPX skew, which jumped from the 12th and 38th percentiles on Nov 11 to the 59th and 67th. The GS vol forecast points to elevated volatility and choppy near-term conditions.
Holiday liquidity is expected to thin. Top-of-book liquidity has stayed robust, but GS sees it trending lower into the holiday season.

Seasonality: since 1990, in the 17 years VIX started mid-November at 18 or higher, VIX was lower by year-end in 14 years, by 3.25 pts on average. SPX's year-end gain was smaller in those years (mean +1.34%, up in 59% of years), the median drawdown within the window is -3.0%, and most gains come after Dec 15.

sector_views.rationale: Institutional investors were the most net sellers of Info Tech again, with the US Info Tech long/short ratio at a record low. Retail dip-buying in semis and mega-cap tech is the offset. This describes flows, not a formal GS rating.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The print was followed by fixed income ETF outflows on Thursday and Friday and by stocks and bonds falling together, which typically leads risk parity funds to cut exposure.

risk_factors: Retail buying slows or reverses. GS says losing this level of support could drastically change the setup for US equities into year-end.
Continued AI-trade and spending concerns, with institutions still net selling tech.
CTA flows are asymmetric today but could flip quickly. In a down tape the 1-month projection is $122.97B of selling, $20.31B of it US.
Thin holiday liquidity and elevated vol, with turbulence expected over the next two weeks.
Stocks and bonds falling together after the hot CPI print, which drives risk parity de-risking.
vol_and_positioning: GS Panic Index is 6.3/10, the 67th percentile on a 1y lookback. It combines 2y weighted percentiles of 1-month S&P implied vol, VIX volatility, S&P 1m put-call skew and the S&P term structure slope (1m vs 3m).
VIX volatility moved from the 12th to the 59th percentile and SPX skew from the 38th to the 67th between Nov 11 and Nov 13 (rolling 2y lookback).

CTAs are short about $10bn of US equities, the lowest since April. Projected 1-week flows: flat tape buyers $22.97B ($9.86B US), up tape buyers $30.78B ($16.1B US), down tape sellers $6.07B ($5.23B US).
Projected 1-month CTA flows: flat tape buyers $13.87B ($8.01B US), up tape buyers $89.1B ($54.04B US), down tape sellers $122.97B ($20.31B US).
Vol control and risk parity sold over $30bn combined over the past week. Vol control may re-risk in December/January if the market calms.
US Fundamental L/S net leverage is at the 4th percentile one-year (45.4%), and the US Info Tech long/short ratio is the lowest in the GS record.
Levered semis ETFs (SOXL, SOXS) show large two-way flow reversals, read by GS as lack of conviction.

tension_points.bull_case: Systematic flows are skewed to the upside for the first time in weeks (CTAs projected to buy about $10bn of US equities over the next week in a flat tape). Retail and corporates have defended their bid, buybacks are running 1.3x prior years with authorizations at $1.52T, foreign flows are returning to the US, and institutional positioning is light enough that a sustained move lower is hard without going higher first.
tension_points.bear_case: Institutions are selling tech and cutting leverage as the AI trade is tested. Vol and skew remain elevated (Panic Index 6.3/10), stocks and bonds fell together after the hot CPI print, and the next two weeks are historically turbulent. Seasonality shows a median drawdown of -3.0% inside the window, and liquidity thins into the holidays.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Retail buying fading or disappointing this week. GS says losing this level of support can drastically change the setup for US equities into year-end.

tension_points.bull_case: CTAs are short about $10bn of US equities, vol has come in from highs and spot is rebounding. They are projected buyers in flat and up tapes, with $54.04B of US buying over 1 month in an up tape.
tension_points.bear_case: In a down tape CTAs are projected sellers of $122.97B over 1 month, $20.31B of it US, and GS notes that the skew can change quickly in this tape.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A down tape over the coming week or month flips CTA flow from asymmetric upside to selling.

theme_stances.key_argument: Light institutional positioning and upside-skewed systematic flows make a sustained move lower hard to sustain without a higher leg first.
theme_stances.evidence: equities will choppily grind moderately higher from here

theme_stances.key_argument: Institutions net sold Info Tech for another week and cut leverage, while the broader AI trade is tested by spending concerns.
theme_stances.evidence: Institutional investors have sold tech and removed leverage from the trade

theme_stances.key_argument: Retail returned with record weekly net buying since Sep 1, concentrated in semis and mega-cap tech, and is a key support for equities.
theme_stances.evidence: Retail has buoyed the market once again as the AI trade is tested
